title: Relief and Drainage Patterns in Eritrea
intro: Relief and Drainage Patterns in Eritrea Deepen Relief and Drainage Patterns in Eritrea with definitions, worked examples, and exam tips in the cards below.

cards.title: 7.1.1 The lowlands
body: A lowland is a land feature with an elevation of less than 1500m.a.s.l.
In Eritrea, there are two major divisions of lowlands separated by the highlands.

cards.title: 7.1.2 The Eastern escarpment
body: The rivers Haddas, Comayli, Endeli, Dandero, Alighede and Labka have cut deep valleys.
The Escarpment is varied and so fascinating.

cards.title: 7.1.3 The highlands
body: The highlands of Eritrea occupy the central portion of the country extending from south to north.
The highlands are divided into six land features.

cards.title: Relief & drainage in Eritrea
body: Highlands, escarpments, western lowlands, coastal plains.
Drainage toward Red Sea or inland systems — know major rivers named in your notes.

cards.title: Drainage basins
body: Watershed / divide separates basins. Tributaries join main river.
Seasonal rivers matter in semi-arid lowlands.

cards.title: Main relief regions
body: Eritrea’s relief includes **highlands**, **escarpments**, **western lowlands**, and **coastal plains**.
Altitude changes temperature and rainfall — highlands are generally cooler than the Danakil/coastal desert heat.
Relief steers where people farm, settle, and build roads.

cards.title: Worked: temperature with height
cards.problem: Why are highland towns often cooler?

steps.text: Temperature generally falls with altitude (~0.6°C per 100 m rule of thumb).

cards.title: Escarpment & lowlands
body: An escarpment is a steep slope joining different elevation levels — erosion and road building are harder here.
Western lowlands often show seasonal watercourses; farming calendars follow rains.
Always link relief → climate → land use in exam answers.

cards.title: 7.2.1 The eastern drainage system
body: The stream finally enters the Red Sea through Marsa Teklai.
Te river Haddas has dissected the Eastern Escarpment into deep gorges.

cards.title: 7.2.2 The western drainage system
body: The longest tributary of the river Anseba is River Zara, which originates from Halhal Highlands.
The river Anseba joins river Barka close to the Sudanese border at Sala where both drain into the Sudan.

cards.title: 7.2.3 Rivers that drain into the Danakil Depression
body: Many of the rivers that drain into the Danakil Depression dry up in the sandy surface.
Endeli originates from the area south of Senafe.

cards.title: Worked: highland advantage
cards.problem: One farming advantage of Eritrean highlands?

steps.text: Cooler temps / often more reliable rains than coastal desert (as in notes).

cards.title: Common mix-ups in Relief and Drainage Patterns in Eritrea
body: Write one idea students often confuse with this topic, then the correct distinction.
Example pattern: “Looks like X, but actually Y because …”
Teaching the difference is better than re-reading the page.

cards.title: Drainage patterns
body: Rivers may drain toward the **Red Sea** or inland systems depending on the watershed.
Seasonal rivers are common in drier lowlands — flow after rains, dry otherwise.
A **drainage basin** is the land drained by a river and its tributaries; a **watershed** divides basins.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: A watershed is best described as…

cards.title: Worked: drainage basin
cards.problem: Define drainage basin and give one human use of rivers.

steps.text: Basin = area drained by a river + tributaries.
Uses: water supply, farming, sometimes transport.

cards.title: 7.3 Lakes in Eritrea
body: In Eritrea, there are no significant natural lakes.
Lake Bordole is located in the Buri Peninsula where salt is extracted.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: Relief west to east: *"Lowlands, Highlands, Escarpment, Coast"* (and the Danakil in the south-east).

cards.title: Map skill
body: On contour maps, close lines = steep; V shapes in contours often point upstream.

cards.title: Relief ↔ effect
head: Region type
Typical effect
rows: cooler; more settlement/farming in many notes

questions.q: The highest peak in the Central Plateau is:
why: The textbook: in the Central (Hamasien) Plateau, 'Emba Tekera, 2579 m above sea level, is the highest peak.'
Emba Soira (3013 m) is in the Eastern Highlands, Hager Nues in the Northern Highlands, Mt Ghini in the Upper Anseba Highlands and Emba Tekillo in the Mereb Trough.
